Assume AC.  Every $R$-oriented rank-$n$ numerable vector bundle over a CW
complex, or over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW type, has a unique
normalized Thom class $u_\xi$, and
$$a\longmapsto\pi^*a\smile u_\xi:H^k(B;R)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$$
for every $k$.  Without a supplied orientation, the canonical twisted form is
$$H^k(B;\mathcal O_R(\xi))\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R).$$
The finite supplied-trivializing-cover theorem is a choice-free special case.

Assume AC.  For ordered oriented bundles $\xi\to B$ and $\eta\to C$ of ranks
$n,m$, the canonical product-pair identification gives
$$u_{\xi\times\eta}=u_\xi\times u_\eta.$$
For bundles over one base, diagonal pullback gives
$$u_{\xi\oplus\eta}=u_\xi\smile u_\eta.$$
Interchanging the ordered summands changes the orientation and the displayed
class by the Koszul sign $(-1)^{nm}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly as in the general Thom theorem, and let
$\xi\to B$ be an $R$-oriented numerable real rank-$n$ vector bundle over a
base in the scope of that theorem. Let $u_\xi\in H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$ be its
normalized Thom class, let
$$j^*:H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)\longrightarrow H^n(D(\xi);R)$$ be the relative-to-absolute map of the pair sequence, and let $s:B\to D(\xi)$ be the zero section. The **Euler class** of $\xi$ is $$e(\xi)=e_{\rm Th}(\xi):=s^*j^*(u_\xi)\in H^n(B;R).$$
This is the class already introduced in
[[def-thom-euler-class-of-an-oriented-vector-bundle]]: on this page we write
$e(\xi)$ for it, and the shorthand $s^*u_\xi$ always means the composite
$s^*j^*(u_\xi)$, the relative-to-absolute map being understood. For rank zero
with supplied orientation $o\in H^0(B;R)$, normalization gives $u_\xi=o$ and
$j$ and $s$ are identities, so
$$e(0_B,o)=o\in H^0(B;R).$$
In particular, the standard unit orientation gives $e(0_B,1)=1$.
For $R=\mathbb F_2$ every real bundle is canonically $\mathbb F_2$-oriented by
[[def-r-oriented-vector-bundle-and-orientation-local-system]], so in that
case $e_2(\xi):=e(\xi)\in H^n(B;\mathbb F_2)$ is defined for every real
bundle in the Thom scope; for $R=\mathbb Z$ the class depends on the chosen
integral orientation, and reversing the orientation negates it.

derivations.claim: Purity and the supported Thom morphism. Put $Y=M\times M$. By [F1] and [F2], $\Delta^!k_Y=\Delta^!\omega_Y[-4d]=\omega_M[-4d]=k_M[-2d]$. The positive orientation identifies the identity of $k_M[-2d]$ with the Thom class in $H^{2d}_{\Delta(M)}(Y;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_M,\Delta^!k_Y[2d])$. Its adjoint is the purity counit $g_\Delta:\Delta_*k_M[-2d]\to k_Y$, equivalently $\Delta_*k_M\to k_Y[2d]$. In a complex normal ball this is the positive generator of the relative disk pair; complex chart transitions preserve that generator. This fixes a global supported morphism through the orientation isomorphism and its counit, rather than inferring equality of arbitrary global maps from their restrictions to balls.

Pullback and cap product on arbitrary supports. Put $S=A\times B$. Proper base change along $F=(q,u)$ identifies $F^*\Delta_*k_M[-2d]$ with $\theta_*k_T[-2d]$, so $F^*g_\Delta$ gives $g_F:\theta_*k_T[-2d]\to k_S$. For a dualizing class $c:k_S\to\omega_S[-n]$, compose $c\circ g_F$ and use $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$ and $\theta^!\omega_S=\omega_T$. The resulting map $k_T\to\omega_T[2d-n]$ is a Borel–Moore class of degree $n-2d$ on $T$. This defines the supported cap operation even if $T$ is singular or has excess dimension; no purity of $\theta$ is asserted. The external product uses $\omega_A\boxtimes\omega_B=\omega_S$: on the supplied finite local product cochain models, compact-support cochains tensor, and their finite-dimensional duals tensor as well, giving this canonical comparison and its restriction compatibility.

Comparison with the exchange mate. For a constructible $C$ on $M$, the mate is the adjoint of $b_!a^*q^!C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^{-1}}u^*q_!q^!C\xrightarrow{u^*\epsilon_q}u^*C$, where $\mathrm{BC}:u^*q_!\xrightarrow{\sim}b_!a^*$ and $\epsilon_q$ is the exceptional counit. To identify its dualizing evaluation with step 2.1, factor $q$ as its graph $\Gamma_q:A\hookrightarrow A\times M$ followed by the second projection. The graph is the pullback of $\Delta$ along $(q,\operatorname{id}_M):A\times M\to M\times M$; its supported orientation map is that pullback of $g_\Delta$. Base change of the graph along $\operatorname{id}_A\times u$ is exactly $\theta$, so its supported orientation map after this second pullback is $g_F$. For the product projection, tensor–Hom evaluation with the relative dualizing factor $\omega_A$ computes the counit; this is the finite product cochain evaluation of step 2.1. Composing the graph counit and that evaluation gives $\epsilon_q$ by the composition-of-counits identity in [F1]. Cartesian pasting therefore makes its base-changed composite exactly $u^*\epsilon_q\circ\mathrm{BC}^{-1}$ above. Taking adjoints and using $q^!k_M=\omega_A[-2d]$ proves that the exchange, paired with the second dualizing class by tensor evaluation, is $c\circ g_F$ under $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$. Every map retains support on $T$ throughout this factorization.

Ordered iterated diagonals. For two ordered smooth middle factors the normal model of the product diagonal is the ordered direct sum of the two complex normal bundles, and on the product of normal coordinate disks the relative cup product of the two positive generators evaluates to $+1$ on the ordered product disk, which is the positive generator of the direct sum; local uniqueness as in step 1.1 and base-change mate pasting as in steps 2.1 and 3.1 therefore give the composed refined operation on every support, in the given order and without an interchange of factors. All real degrees involved are even, so reordering the two complex summands introduces no sign: the only possible sign is $(-1)^{(2d_1)(2d_2)}=+1$. The equivariant form holds verbatim by [F3], which supplies the same localization, exchange and normalized orientation clauses in $D^b_{G,c}$, with $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$ rather than a quotient-stack shift.

Zero sections and Euler classes. Let $V\to X$ have complex rank $c$ and zero section $s$. In a bundle chart the normal pair is the product with $(\mathbb C^c,\mathbb C^c\setminus\{0\})$, so the same relative cochain calculation gives $s^!k_V=k_X[-2c]$ and its positive supported counit; here $c$ is the bundle rank, independently of $\dim X$. These local orientations glue because the complex transition matrices preserve the positive fiber generator. On bases in the Thom scope of [F5], this supported class is the normalized Thom class by uniqueness. Pulling its relative-to-absolute image back by $s$ gives $e(V)$ by [F5]. Applying the supported cap construction of step 2.1 after $s_*$ restricts that class to the zero section; the projection formula thus gives $s^!s_*z=e(V)\cap z$. The same counit and base-change identities give its proper-pushforward and refined-pullback compatibility; the equivariant version uses [F3]. Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ for $p\ge1$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$ for $p\ge0$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_m\to Z_p$. In general this action nerve has no augmentation to
$X$: already the two faces $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$ are projection and
action and need not agree. For a free action with principal quotient
$P\to P/G$, its action nerve is instead augmented over $P/G$, as in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_p)\to H^j(A_m)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups acting algebraically on a separated finite-type complex
algebraic variety $X$, and let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero. For
bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in the equivariant category
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]:

1. every $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ is
   finite-dimensional over $k$ and vanishes for all sufficiently negative $m$;
2. for every field extension $k\to K$ of characteristic-zero fields, the
   canonical map
   $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$
   is an isomorphism, natural in $A$ and $B$ and compatible with shifts and
   with Yoneda composition;
3. coefficient extension commutes with the coherent six operations, normalized
   Verdier duality, perverse truncation and intermediate extension on these
   bounded constructible objects.

The total Ext space $\bigoplus_m\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)$ need not be
finite-dimensional, and simplicity is not asserted to be preserved under
coefficient extension.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: The adjunction chain. Write $p:Z_{ij}\to X_i$ and $q:Z_{ij}\to X_j$ for the projections and put $t=r+d_j-d_i$. Removing the source shift by $[-d_i]$ and using the adjunction $f_{i!}\dashv f_i^!$ of [F1] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_E(f_{i!}k_i,f_{j!}k_j[t])=\operatorname{Hom}_{X_i}(k_i,f_i^!f_{j!}k_j[t])$. In the Cartesian square with lower arrow $f_j$ and right arrow $f_i$, the extraordinary proper base change of [F1] gives $f_i^!f_{j!}k_j=p_*q^!k_j$, because both maps are proper and the square is Cartesian; the adjunction $p^*\dashv p_*$ then identifies the group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{Z_{ij}}(k_Z,q^!k_j[t])$. This is the complete cornerwise chain and it is valid for every integer $r$, including negative $r$.

Orientation and the degree. The smooth orientation of [F1] on the smooth pure $d_j$-dimensional source $X_j$ says $k_{X_j}=\omega_{X_j}[-2d_j]$, and dualizing transitivity for $q$ gives $q^!k_{X_j}=q^!\omega_{X_j}[-2d_j]=\omega_{Z_{ij}}[-2d_j]$. Substituting $t=r+d_j-d_i$, the group of step 1.1 is $\operatorname{Hom}(k_Z,\omega_Z[r-d_i-d_j])$, which is exactly $H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k)$ in the normalization of [F3]. At a finite free smooth approximation of dimension offset $b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the space $X_j\times_GU$ is smooth of complex dimension $d_j+b$ while the descended complex retains the shift $d_j$, so the identical calculation gives ordinary Borel–Moore degree $d_i+d_j+2b-r$; removing $2b$ gives the stated equivariant degree, and no stack-dimension shift is inserted into $\omega_X^G$.

Naturality, linearity and finiteness. Every map in the chain of steps 1.1 and 2.1 is an adjunction, base-change or orientation map supplied naturally by [F1], so the composite is natural in constructible coefficient morphisms before the smooth orientation is applied and is compatible with composition of the $f_i$. By [F2] these maps commute with the approximation transition pullbacks on the bounded ranges, so the composite induces an isomorphism in each stable degree; coherent scalar pullback from the base point together with the projection formula of [F1] gives equivariant-cohomology linearity. Degreewise finiteness is exactly the conclusion of [F4] for bounded algebraically constructible objects, and it is asserted nowhere that the direct sum over all degrees is finite-dimensional. Smoothness of the sources is used only for the orientation in step 2.1, and properness only in the base change and in the identification $f_{i!}=f_{i*}$; no semismallness, decomposition theorem, purity or smoothness of $E$ or of the fiber products $Z_{ij}$ is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ for $p\ge1$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$ for $p\ge0$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_m\to Z_p$. In general this action nerve has no augmentation to
$X$: already the two faces $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$ are projection and
action and need not agree. For a free action with principal quotient
$P\to P/G$, its action nerve is instead augmented over $P/G$, as in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_p)\to H^j(A_m)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that

derivations.claim: The geometry and the cohomology of the projective line. The fiber products are $Z_{12}=Z_{21}=\mathbb P^1$. By [F3] its Schubert CW structure has one $0$-cell and one $2$-cell, so the cellular cochain complex is $k\oplus k[-2]$. By [F4] it computes singular cohomology, and [F6] identifies this with constant-sheaf cohomology. Choosing cocycles representing the two generators gives a quasi-isomorphism $k\oplus k[-2]\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$. Hence $L_2\simeq k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ and $L_1=k$.

The two classes and their composites. The unit $\alpha:k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ includes the degree-zero summand, generating $\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)=k$. Evaluation at a point projects to that summand; its shift $\beta:L_2\to k[1]$ generates $\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_2,L_1)=k$, since $\operatorname{Hom}(k[-2],k)=0$. Therefore $\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$. The reverse composite $\alpha[1]\circ\beta$ is also nonzero: it is the projector of $L_2=k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ onto $k[1]$, and is neither zero nor $\operatorname{id}_{L_2}$.

The convolution check. Apply [F2] with $(i,j,k)=(1,2,1)$ and degrees $r=-1$, $s=1$ to the composable pair $\alpha:L_1\to L_2[r]$ and $\beta:L_2\to L_1[s]$: since $\beta[r]\circ\alpha=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ by step 2.1, the product theorem gives $\Phi_{11}^{0}(\operatorname{id}_k)=\Phi_{12}^{-1}(\alpha)*\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)$, so $\alpha*\beta=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention, and the right-hand side is the convolution product of [F1]. The corner degrees are $d_1+d_2-r=2$ for $\alpha$ and $d_2+d_1-s=0$ for $\beta$.

The geometric product. The adjunction chain of [F1] sends $\alpha$ to $\operatorname{id}_{k_{\mathbb P^1}}$, hence to the positive fundamental class $[\mathbb P^1]$. Write $i:\mathrm{pt}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^1$ for the evaluation point. Evaluation is the global-sections image of $k_{\mathbb P^1}\to i_*k$, and its adjoint under $R\Gamma\dashv a^!$, $a:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{pt}$, is the composite $k_{\mathbb P^1}\to i_*k=i_*i^!\omega_{\mathbb P^1}\to\omega_{\mathbb P^1}$, with the last arrow the proper trace. Thus $\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)=i_*[\mathrm{pt}]$ with coefficient $+1$. Geometrically $\mathbb P^1\times\{i\}$ meets the middle diagonal of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ transversely at $(i,i)$; the map from its tangent line to the complex normal line of the diagonal is an isomorphism, preserving the real orientation. The positive Thom cap of [F5] therefore gives that point with multiplicity $+1$, and proper pushforward to $Z_{11}=\mathrm{pt}$ gives $[\mathrm{pt}]$. This computes $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$, with middle degree drop $2$ and no permutation sign, agreeing with step 3.1. It verifies a transverse instance of the calculus, not its general nontransverse case. AC is inherited through [A1].
